subject: Learning Methods
title: Generative Note-Taking
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Generative Note-Taking.

hook.text: She didn't just write what the professor said. She added questions, connections, and her own reactions in the margins.

buildup.text: Generative note-taking means adding your own thinking to the source material: questions, connections, and summaries.

discovery.text: The more you transform the information during note-taking, the deeper the encoding.

twist.text: Generative notes take longer to write. But the extra minutes during capture save hours of review later.

climax.text: For every fact you note, add one question or one connection. This small habit doubles the encoding power.

punchline.text: Add your own thinking. Notes with connections stick longer.

quiz.question: What makes generative note-taking more effective than passive recording?
options: Adding personal questions and connections deepens encoding
